analyst_view.overall: Leaders Lazio (32 points from 12 games, four wins and a draw in their last five, latest a 3-0 win over Lecce) travel to 13th-placed Torino, who have lost three of their last five and went down 1-0 at Napoli on 21 November. Lazio lose Nuno Tavares and Sutalo to thigh injuries (Tavares back in early December), but Zaccagni and Marusic have recovered and should be available, according to Sky Sport as cited by Lazio Channel. Torino came out of Naples with three doubts: Belghali (knee), Ismajli (possible broken finger) and Biraghi (muscle fatigue), none ruled out yet. The numbers already count Lazio's strong scoring form and both sides' recent low card counts; no referee is named yet, and there is no midweek European game for either side in what I read.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, with Lazio's 17 goals in their last six already lifting the away side (+4%). Lazio lose an attacking full-back in Nuno Tavares but get Zaccagni back, and Torino's possible absences (Ismajli, Biraghi) are only doubts so far, so the two roughly cancel out. I stay at about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners, already lifting Lazio for their recent 33 corners in six games. Tavares' overlapping runs on the left are a source of Lazio crosses, but Zaccagni returning on that flank largely makes up for it. Nothing points clearly either way, so I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, already cut by about 9% for each side because both have been booked less than usual lately. No referee has been named yet, and a home side chasing a leader usually commits fouls without the edge of a derby. I stay at about 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots, already moving Lazio up (+9%) for their recent volume and Torino down (-6%) for theirs. Torino's struggles at home and Lazio's form are counted; the injury news on both sides is mostly in defence and mostly doubts. I stay at about 24.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target, with Lazio's 32 on target in their last six already counted (+9%). With Zaccagni back Lazio keep their main creative winger, while Torino's attack has no reported new absences. I stay at about 8.4.
